# Out-of-bounds writes in BMP RLE and TIFF strip decoding

JuicyPixels contains independent out-of-bounds writes reachable from ordinary
image decoding (`Codec.Picture.decodeImage` and the format-specific decoders):

1. **BMP `BI_RLE8`/`BI_RLE4`** (`Codec.Picture.Bitmap.decodeImageY8RLE`): the
   pixel buffer size is computed with 32-bit `Int32` arithmetic and wraps to a
   zero-length allocation for large headers; end-of-line and vertical-delta
   control codes move the destination cursor without a bound, and the
   horizontal delta jump is unclamped. Every run writes attacker-chosen bytes
   through `M.unsafeWrite` at the cursor position — negative offsets before
   the raster, arbitrary offsets against a wrapped allocation, and up to 255
   bytes past it.
2. **TIFF uncompressed/PackBits contiguous strips**
   (`Codec.Picture.Tiff.gatherStrips`, `copyByteString`, `unpackPackBit`):
   strip copies have no destination bound and the per-strip size computation
   wraps negative for strips starting past the raster, so excess strips copy
   attacker-chosen bytes past the end of the allocated raster.

Impact: heap memory adjacent to the decoded image is corrupted with
attacker-selected values and offsets through maliciously crafted BMP or TIFF
files. Beyond corruption, exploitation primitives were demonstrated
end-to-end on GHC 9.6 / linux-amd64: a crafted BMP deterministically crashed
the process via the wrapped allocation; against a warp-based service a single
uploaded BMP overwrote another request's in-memory session blob, observed in
the victim's own HTTP response (12 of 12 cycles); and with heap grooming the
write primitive was used to redirect a lazily-evaluated top-level `String`
passed to `callCommand`, executing attacker-supplied commands (3 of 3 runs).
These are relative-offset primitives: the demonstrated RCE depends on heap
layout and linkage and is not a guaranteed arbitrary-address write.

The fix, released in 3.3.10, validates the declared pixel count centrally in
`decodeBitmapWithPaletteAndMetadata` (cap 2^29 pixels, i.e. 2 GiB of RGBA8),
computes all decoder buffer sizes in exact 64-bit `Int` arithmetic, clips
out-of-bounds BMP RLE writes to the raster (zero-filling skipped pixels,
matching the clipping behaviour of the non-RLE decoders and the Windows WIC
decoder), bounds TIFF strip copies at the destination buffer, and clamps
strip counts at the raster boundary. Malformed-but-decodable files keep
decoding instead of failing.

Residual risk in 3.3.10: the shared GIF/TIFF LZW decoder
(`Codec.Picture.Gif.Internal.LZW`) retains an unguarded single-byte
KwKwK write reachable from the same TIFF/GIF decode paths; it is
documented as a follow-up and is not addressed by this release.

Credit: external vulnerability report by Akash Sebastian (@akashseb) and Tomer
Fichman (irregular).
summary: Out-of-bounds writes in BMP RLE and TIFF strip decoding
